learnings.title: GitHub: self-serve confirmed hands-on, plus an undocumented callback parameter
learnings.detail: A tester registered an OAuth App and completed authorization in a few minutes with no review, as the guide says. The callback also carried iss=https://github.com/login/oauth (RFC 9207), which GitHub's OAuth docs don't mention. We added it as a Tested nuance.

learnings.title: Slack's 'Create new app' dialog changed; our checklist was out of date
learnings.detail: The dialog now offers AI agent, Starter app, From a manifest and Blank app. 'From scratch' is gone. The curated Slack guide already said 'Blank app' because it was built from current docs, but our manual checklist said 'From scratch' and confused the tester. Creating a new workspace also pushed paid-plan upsells, which a developer can skip by staying on the Free plan or using a Developer Program sandbox.

learnings.title: Slack: install worked hands-on; the settings form accepted an http:// redirect URL
learnings.detail: The OAuth v2 install into the tester's own workspace worked with no review, as the guide says. But the OAuth & Permissions page saved http://example.com/x even though Slack's docs and our guide said HTTPS is required. We corrected the guide to separate what the docs say from what the form enforces, and left the authorize-time behaviour as an open question.

learnings.title: Google: Gmail scopes are hidden until the Gmail API is enabled
learnings.detail: The tester couldn't find any gmail scopes under Data Access. The console only lists scopes for enabled APIs ('Only scopes for enabled APIs are listed below'). The curated guide already has 'Enable the Gmail, Calendar and Drive APIs' as its own step, but our shorter manual checklist skipped it, so the checklist was fixed. Lesson: order matters, and a skipped prerequisite step looks like a missing feature.

learnings.title: Google: scope tiers confirmed hands-on; warning screen differs for test users
learnings.detail: The console labelled gmail.send sensitive and gmail.readonly restricted, as the guide said. Test users see a milder 'currently being tested' warning with a direct Continue button, not the Advanced > Go to app path a community source described. We corrected the blocker. Authorization works in Testing mode immediately even for a restricted scope; the cost comes later, at verification time.

learnings.title: Agent alone vs. human-verified: right on verdicts for well-documented providers, but it misses recent policy changes
learnings.detail: Run with no help, the live agent matched the curated verdict for GitHub and Google. For Slack it missed the 2025 rate-limit change for unlisted apps, which is the main thing a Slack agent builder needs to know, and so under-rated the difficulty. It also borrowed Google's 'sensitive' scope vocabulary for GitHub and Slack. The fact-checker caught 2 of these wrong claims. Takeaway: agent guides are a good first draft and clearly labelled as such; recent changelog-level changes are where human curation adds the most.

agreed: Self-serve with no review; same difficulty (1/5) and production estimate
Org OAuth access restrictions are the main real-world blocker
GitHub recommends GitHub Apps over OAuth Apps for fine-grained permissions
missed: The August 2026 change: new OAuth Apps get 8-hour expiring tokens plus refresh tokens
GitHub returns 404, not 403, for blocked private repos, so failures look like missing data
SAML SSO orgs need an active SSO session per token
wrong: Labelled repo, workflow and hook scopes 'sensitive'; GitHub has no sensitive/restricted scope tiers (that's Google's model)
One claim about rate-limit monitoring was not supported by its cited page (the fact-checker caught it and downgraded it)

agreed: Public distribution needs no review; Marketplace listing does
Exact redirect URI matching and scope-union behaviour on reinstall
The published app's configuration locks after listing
missed: The 2025 rate-limit cut for non-Marketplace apps: conversations.history/replies drop to 1 request per minute (15 messages). This is the main reason the curated guide rates Slack 3/5 'limited until reviewed', not 2/5 self-serve
The 10-active-workspace prerequisite before Marketplace submission, and the review length (up to 10 weeks)
Classic apps stop working on Nov 16, 2026
wrong: Tier: 'self_serve', difficulty 2, and 'weeks' for Marketplace, versus 'limited until reviewed', 3, and 2-4 months
Called channels:history 'sensitive'; the fact-checker found the cited page doesn't say so and downgraded it to Inferred

agreed: gmail.send sensitive and gmail.readonly restricted, both later confirmed hands-on in the console
Restricted scopes need CASA; Testing-mode refresh tokens expire after 7 days
All 6 fact-checked claims supported by their sources
missed: The 100-user cap for unverified apps lasts the project's lifetime and can't be reset
Google's 2026 Workspace policy rules for AI agents (user confirmation of tool calls, prompt-injection defenses)
Cheaper paths by scope tier (drive.file and non-sensitive scopes avoid review); CASA cost range
wrong: Nothing material; its timeline ('several weeks or longer') was vaguer than the scope-based ranges
